settings.heroImageAlt: Aisha Ali Muhammad, Technical Project Manager

hero.text: I bridge clients and developers across GoHighLevel, WordPress, automation and digital platforms, from the first requirement to final handover.

about.title: I connect business goals with technical execution.
about.statement: I’m a Technical Project Manager with {{experience}} years of experience coordinating digital projects, managing client relationships and guiding development teams. My role isn’t to write the code. It’s to understand it well enough to make informed decisions, set clear expectations and deliver the right solution.
paragraphs: My work spans GoHighLevel CRM systems, WordPress websites, marketing automation, SaaS and AI-related platforms, online course platforms and e-commerce projects.
I turn client conversations into clear tasks, help developers move without guesswork, and check every deliverable against what was agreed.
about.linkText: Let’s talk about your project or role

services.title: From the first call to final handover.
services.lead: Five things I take care of on every project, so clients feel heard and developers know exactly what to build.

items.title: Client Communication & Requirements
items.text: I work directly with clients to understand their goals, gather requirements, clarify expectations and turn discussions into actionable development tasks.

items.title: Technical Project Coordination
items.text: I evaluate implementation options, discuss alternative approaches and work with developers to agree on the most suitable solution.

items.title: Development Team Management
items.text: Structured task descriptions, requirements shared on Slack, quick answers to questions, managed dependencies and steady follow-ups.

items.title: Project Tracking & Delivery
items.text: Tasks, timelines and progress tracked in ClickUp and Airtable, with client timesheets maintained and deliverables coordinated.

items.title: Quality & Requirement Validation
items.text: I review completed work against the agreed requirements, flag discrepancies and coordinate revisions before anything reaches the client.

process.title: A clear path from requirements to delivery.
process.lead: Six steps keep every project organised, transparent and moving forward.

steps.title: Discover
steps.text: Understand the client’s objectives, requirements, priorities and expected outcomes.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.text: Review technical requirements, identify dependencies, assess feasibility and discuss approaches.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Break requirements into clear tasks, set priorities and document acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Coordinate
steps.text: Brief developers, clarify requirements, resolve blockers and keep stakeholders updated.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Validate completed work against requirements, collect feedback and coordinate revisions.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.text: Coordinate final delivery, confirm open items and keep documentation and timesheets up to date.

cards.title: Technically informed decisions
cards.text: I understand the platforms behind the projects I manage.

cards.title: Clear communication
cards.text: Client discussions become structured, understandable tasks.

cards.title: Solution-oriented thinking
cards.text: When the first approach won’t work, I find practical alternatives.

cards.title: Organized execution
cards.text: Tasks, documentation, timelines and updates stay in order.

cards.title: Client-focused delivery
cards.text: Agreed requirements and business goals stay at the centre.

contact.title: Let’s start the conversation.
contact.lead: Hiring for a technical project manager role, or need someone to organise a digital project? Share a few details and I’ll get back to you.
